claims.value: Pacioli describes the Last Supper in the dedicatory letter of De divina proportione
claims.statement: Luca Pacioli refers to the painting of the Last Supper in the dedicatory letter to Ludovico Sforza of his manuscript De divina proportione, describing the apostles intent at the voice of the truth. The date of the dedication is reported as 9 February 1498 by some accounts and the treatise's conclusion as 14 December 1497 by others (see open questions). The mention indicates the composition was visible by then; it does not say the painting was finished.

claims.value: Bandello's account of Leonardo at work (later narrative source)
claims.statement: Matteo Bandello's dedicatory letter to novella I.58 of his Novelle (first printed 1554) describes Leonardo working on the Last Supper, sometimes painting from dawn to dusk and at other times only adding a few strokes. It is a narrative source printed some sixty years after the event; that Bandello was an eyewitness as a young novice at the Grazie is his own claim and an interpretation of its value.

claims.statement: A start around 1495 and completion by 1498 is the common scholarly range: the end rests on the Pacioli mention and the 1497 memorandum showing the work unfinished in June 1497; the start rests on context (Montorfano's 1495 date, the refectory works). Neither end is fixed by a document of the painting's beginning or completion.

open_questions: Exact text and archival locator of the 29 June 1497 memorandum (Villata number).
Date of Pacioli's dedicatory letter: 9 February 1498 (often cited) or the 14 December 1497 conclusion date? Which codex carries which date?
Is there any document for the start of work or for a formal commission? Other 1496 to 1498 documents (Leonardo's own letter of complaint to Ludovico; payment notes) should be listed from Villata.
When did Bandello write the I.58 dedicatory letter, and was he at the Grazie in the 1490s?

background.text: The Last Supper is a mural painting by the Italian High Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, dated to c. 1495, 1498, housed in the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Italy. The painting represents the scene of the Last Supper of Jesus with the Twelve Apostles, as it is told in the Gospel of John, specifically the moment after Jesus announces that one of his apostles will betray him. Its handling of space, mastery of perspective, treatment of motion and complex display of human emotion has made it one of the Western world's most recognizable paintings and among Leonardo's most celebrated works. Some commentators consider it pivotal in inaugurating the transition into what is now termed the High Renaissance.

Il Cenacolo, noto anche come l'Ultima Cena, è un dipinto parietale, definito spesso impropriamente come un affresco, ottenuto con una tecnica mista "a secco" su intonaco (460×880 cm) di Leonardo da Vinci, databile al 1494-1498 e realizzato su commissione di Ludovico il Moro nel refettorio del convento adiacente al santuario di Santa Maria delle Grazie a Milano.
La Cène de Léonard de Vinci est une peinture murale à la détrempe de 460 × 880 cm, réalisée de 1495 à 1498 pour le réfectoire du couvent dominicain de Santa Maria delle Grazie à Milan.
